paper.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit with finite action sets (minimax regret R(T;n,d))
unmapped: Action sets A_t of size at most n chosen obliviously by an adversary before the policy runs and vary over time
noise independent centered sub-Gaussian with variance proxy 1
settings.definition_quote: At each time period $t$, a \emph{policy} $\pi$ is presented with an \emph{action set} $\mathcal A_t=\{x_{it}\}\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d: \|x\|_2\leq 1\}$ ... An adversary will choose the action sets $\mathcal A_1,\cdots,\mathcal A_T$ \emph{before} the policy is executed ... receives a reward $r_t=x_{it}^\top\theta + \eps_t$, where $\{\eps_t\}$ are independent centered sub-Gaussian random variables with variance proxy $1$

settings.name_in_paper: Linear bandit with infinite, time-varying action spaces
unmapped: Closed infinite action sets A_t in unit ball chosen obliviously and changing over time
settings.definition_quote: there exists a bandit instance with regression model $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, $\|\theta\|_2\leq 1$ and closed action spaces $\mathcal A_1,\cdots,\mathcal A_T\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq 1\}$, $|\mathcal A_t|=\infty$

symbols.n: maximum number of actions per round
symbols.gamma_c: some positive constant exponent of the iterated log factor

source.label: thm:upper-finite
source.quote: For any $n<\infty$, the minimax regret $\mathfrak R(T;n,d)$ can be asymptotically upper bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log(nT))\cdot O(\sqrt{dT(\log T)(\log n)})$.

results.notes: Stated as minimax regret bound; achieved by VCL-SupLinUCB (Section 2). Remark: poly(loglog(nT)) = (loglog(nT))^gamma.

bound.regime: n <= 2^(d/2), T >= d*(log2 n)^(1+epsilon) for constant epsilon>0

symbols.n: maximum number of actions per round
symbols.epsilon: small positive constant (not accuracy); Omega hides constants depending on it

extra_assumptions: Gaussian noise used in hard instances

source.label: thm:lower-finite
source.quote: For any small constant $\epsilon > 0$, and any $n,d, $ such that $n \leq 2^{d/2}$ and $T \geq d (\log_2 n)^{1+\epsilon}$, the minimax regret $\mathfrak R(T;n,d)$ can be asymptotically lower bounded by $\Omega(1)\cdot\sqrt{dT(\log n)\log (T/d)}$.

extra_assumptions: Gaussian noise with variance 1 in hard instances

source.label: thm:LB-n-eq-expd
source.quote: Suppose $T\geq d^5$ and $n=2^{d/2}$. Then $\mathfrak R(T;n,d) = \Omega(1)\cdot d\sqrt{T\log T}$.

bound.regime: T >= d^(2+eps_c), n = 2^(d/2), d sufficiently large

extra_assumptions: Gaussian noise with variance 1 in hard instances

source.label: thm:lb-n-eq-expd-strengthened
source.quote: For any small constant $\epsilon > 0$ and sufficiently large $d$, suppose $T\geq d^{2+\eps}$ and $n=2^{d/2}$. Then $\mathfrak R(T;n,d) = \Omega(1)\cdot d\sqrt{\epsilon T\log T}$.

results.notes: Numbered as Theorem 4 assuming shared counter with lemmas; actual printed number may differ.

source.label: cor:infinite-action
source.quote: For any policy $\pi$, there exists a bandit instance with regression model $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, $\|\theta\|_2\leq 1$ and closed action spaces $\mathcal A_1,\cdots,\mathcal A_T\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq 1\}$, $|\mathcal A_t|=\infty$, such that for sufficiently large $T$, $\mathbb E[R^T] = \Omega(d\sqrt{T\log T}).$

results.notes: Presumably requires T >= d^{2+eps} as inherited from Theorem 4; stated only 'sufficiently large T'.
